title: Almond-flour sandwich loaf
summary: A sliceable, sturdy sandwich loaf from almond flour and psyllium that toasts well.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and line a 23 × 13 cm (9 × 5 in) loaf pan with parchment.
Whisk the almond flour, psyllium, coconut flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
Add the egg whites, egg, lemon juice and olive oil and stir briefly, then pour in the boiling water and mix vigorously until it forms a smooth, thick dough.
With wet hands, shape into a log and press into the pan, smoothing the top. Score a line down the middle.
Bake 65–75 minutes, until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. If the top browns early, cover loosely with foil.
Cool completely in the pan, at least 1 hour, before slicing; cut warm, the crumb is gummy.
tips: Psyllium gives this dough a bread-like chew; brands differ, and some darken the crumb purple-grey — it is harmless.
Slice the whole loaf and freeze it; toast slices straight from frozen.

origin.history: The tall, square-sided pan loaf became the standard sandwich bread with industrial baking. Pre-sliced bread was first sold commercially in 1928 by a bakery in Chillicothe, Missouri, using Otto Rohwedder's slicing machine. This grain-free loaf is a modern low-carb imitation of that everyday bread.
